title_en: How Family Businesses Should Plan for Generational Success
title_zh: 家族企业应如何规划代际传承 | FX Demalman、Tucker York
subtitle_zh: 高盛两位业务掌门人从企业与家族两端，谈家族企业代际传承与继任规划的长期主义。
summary_zh: 本期 Goldman Sachs Exchanges 中，Allison Nathan 请来两位从相反两端看家族企业的嘉宾：EMEA 主席兼投资与银行部门主席 FX Demalman（企业侧，负责大型家族企业与家族办公室 family office 覆盖），以及全球财富管理主管 Tucker York（家族侧）。开篇点出惊人事实：家族仍持重要股份的企业创造全球约 70% 经济产出、60% 就业，但只有约三成传到第二代、约一成传到第三代。Demalman 引用《Honoring Legacy》报告补充：美国有超 3200 万家家族企业、占比逾 80%，欧洲在奢侈品、航运、消费品等行业由家族控股，亚洲则有大型家族财团（family conglomerate）；家族所有者往往持长期视角、是自律的资本配置者，平均表现优于非家族企业。核心命题落在代际交接（generational transition）：创始人须就两件事决断——家族成员是否及以何角色参与日常经营，以及所有权如何跨代传承（平均分配、退出机制、冲突治理，或引入第三方投资人乃至公开市场作约束）。两人强调第一代家族与企业利益高度一致，随代际推移会分歧，须及早厘清；只有约一半家族企业有继任计划、三分之一真正写下来。收束于长期主义：非凡家族做的是押在单一公司上的集中赌注，穿越周期持续在场、增持，是通向巨大价值创造的制胜配方，但也极其冒险。
description: How Family Businesses Should Plan for Generational Success

turns.en: Welcome to Goldman Sachs Exchanges. I'm Allison Nathan. Here's the number that surprised me when I first read it. Companies where a family still holds a significant stake produce 70% of the world's economic output and 60% of its jobs.
turns.zh: 欢迎收听高盛《Exchanges》。我是 Allison Nathan。有个数字我第一次读到时就觉得很惊讶——家族仍然持有重要股份的企业，创造了全球 70% 的经济产出和 60% 的就业。

turns.en: But only 3 in 10 reach a second generation, and only about 1 in 10 reaches a third. So why is that? To help me work through that, I'm joined by two people who see opposite ends of this.
turns.zh: 但只有十分之三能传到第二代，只有大约十分之一能传到第三代。这到底是为什么？为了帮我理清这个问题，我请来了两位从相反两端看这件事的人。

turns.en: FX Demalman is chairman of Goldman Sachs Emia and chairman of Invest and Banking. He also leads the firm's coverage of large family-owned companies and family offices, which means he's on the corporate side of the table, the capital raises, the IPOs, the sales, and the successions.
turns.zh: FX Demalman 是高盛 EMEA（欧洲、中东和非洲区）的主席，也是投资与银行部门的主席。他还负责牵头高盛对大型家族企业和家族办公室（family office）的服务覆盖——也就是说他坐在企业这一侧：融资、IPO、出售，还有传承交接。

turns.en: Tucker York chairs our global wealth management business. He's on the other side, the families, their balance sheets, and the next generation, once that capital is created.
turns.zh: Tucker York 掌管我们全球财富管理业务。他在另一侧——家族本身、他们的资产负债表，以及当这些财富创造出来之后的下一代。

turns.en: FX Tucker, welcome to Exchanges. Thank you, Allison. Good to be here. Thank you, Allison. That's happy to have you both. So FX, let's just start with some context here on the size and the scope and the impact of family-owned businesses.
turns.zh: FX、Tucker，欢迎来到《Exchanges》。谢谢你，Allison，很高兴来到这里。谢谢你，Allison。很高兴有你们两位。那 FX，我们先铺垫一些背景，聊聊家族企业在规模、覆盖面和影响力上的情况。

turns.en: I gave a few stats to start us off, but maybe provide a bit more color on that for us. The statistics you quoted are those we included in our recently published report on honoring legacy, which are global statistics.
turns.zh: 我开头引用了几个数字，也许你能再给我们补充一些细节。你引用的那些统计，正是我们最近发布的《Honoring Legacy》（致敬传承）报告里所包含的，是全球层面的数据。

turns.en: We did dig a little bit deeper into some of the statistics and see how they apply to differ around the world. And what we found is that there is an enormous space on family-owned businesses in all major regions.
turns.zh: 我们确实对一些统计做了更深入的挖掘，看它们在不同地区的应用有何差异。我们发现，在所有主要区域，家族企业都占据着非常大的比重。

turns.en: In the U.S., for instance, there are over 32 million family-owned businesses, which represent over 80% of all businesses. Those account for over 60% of GDP and over 60% of the overall workforce.
turns.zh: 比如说在美国，有超过 3200 万家家族企业，占所有企业的 80% 以上，贡献了超过 60% 的 GDP 和超过 60% 的整体就业人口。

turns.en: If you move from the private company world to the public company world, around 35% of the 4 to 500 companies are family-controlled or have a significant family owner, which is a substantial base.
turns.zh: 如果你从私营企业的世界转到上市公司，大约 35% 的《财富》400 到 500 强企业是家族控股，或者有重要的家族股东，这是一个相当庞大的基数。

turns.en: As you move to Europe, there are significant industries that have leaders, companies that are leading the industry, that have other family-controlled or significant family shareholder in luxury goods, in beauty and cosmetics, in shipping, in consumer goods, in retail, in telco, in business services, in industrial, in defense, in numerous other sectors.
turns.zh: 到了欧洲，很多重要行业里的领军企业——那些引领整个行业的公司——都是家族控股或有重要的家族股东，涵盖奢侈品、美妆、航运、消费品、零售、电信、商业服务、工业、国防，以及众多其他领域。

turns.en: The size and scale and the success of some of these entrepreneurs has been outstanding. And as you move to Asia, there are countries where you have very large family conglomerate that control many sectors of the economy that are very diversified, not only vertically, but also horizontally.
turns.zh: 这些企业家的规模、体量和所取得的成功都非常突出。到了亚洲，在一些国家，有非常大的家族财团（family conglomerate），掌控着经济的许多部门，而且多元化程度很高，不只是纵向的，还有横向的。

turns.en: And you see many of those in India, in Korea, and in numerous other Asian countries where the role that these families play is significant to the economy, but also in their ability to create new businesses and innovate in all the fields where they operate.
turns.zh: 在印度、韩国和许多其他亚洲国家你都能看到很多这样的例子，这些家族扮演的角色对经济意义重大，同时他们在各自涉足的所有领域里，创造新企业和创新的能力也很强。

turns.en: Those numbers are actually absolutely staggering, and I don't think most people think about businesses in that way. If we think about the family-owned businesses, how does the fact of them being family-owned affect how they run?
turns.zh: 这些数字确实非常惊人，我想大多数人平时不会这样去看待企业。如果我们谈家族企业，'家族所有'这个事实会如何影响他们的经营？

turns.en: And how they operate if you're inside the business? Well, in the world family-owned, there is the word owned. And therefore, each of these businesses tend to be owned or partly owned by an individual or a family that, on average, tend to be both invested economically, financially, but also emotionally in the business and very engaged.
turns.zh: 以及从企业内部看，他们是如何运作的？那么，在 'family-owned'（家族所有）这个词里，有一个 'owned'（拥有）。所以这些企业往往是由某个人或某个家族拥有或部分拥有，而这些家族通常在经济上、财务上投入其中，同时在情感上也投入很深，参与也非常紧密。

turns.en: And so we find in our interactions with many of these entrepreneurs that they tend to take a very long-term view on their business. They tend to be rigorous stewards of their management team.
turns.zh: 所以在我们与很多这类企业家的接触中，我们发现他们往往对自己的企业持非常长期的视角，往往对自己的管理团队是严格的守护者。

turns.en: They tend to be disciplined allocator of capital, and they also tend to be prudent with respect to the decision they make, including the investment decision and their use of leverage.
turns.zh: 他们往往是自律的资本配置者，在做决策时也比较审慎，包括投资决策和他们对杠杆的使用。

turns.en: And on balance and statistic that we have access to show that these businesses when family control, on average, tend to outperform non-family control businesses.
turns.zh: 总的来说，我们能拿到的统计数据表明，当企业由家族控股时，平均表现往往优于非家族控股的企业。

turns.en: Tucker, let me bring you into the conversation because you're sitting with these families day-to-day. Again, let me ask you a different version of the question.
turns.zh: Tucker，我来把你拉进对话，因为你每天都在和这些家族打交道。同样，我想问你这个问题的另一个版本。

turns.en: How does the fact that these businesses are family-owned impact the way they invest? I'll take a step back saying that I agree that the numbers are staggering when you think about the family connectivity to business and GDP, etc.
turns.zh: 这些企业是家族所有，会如何影响他们的投资方式？我想先退一步说，我同意那些数字确实惊人，尤其是当你把家族与企业、GDP 等的关联放在一起看时。

turns.en: It's worth putting that in context. In the history of civilization, it used to be a much higher percentage than that. It's only in the last couple of years where we have more of a corporate structure and the scale that comes from that kind of more permanent capital that comes around that that's led to this.
turns.zh: 把这放到背景里看是有价值的。在文明史上，这个比例曾经远比现在高得多。只是在最近这些年，我们才更多地采用公司制结构，以及这种结构带来的更长久资本所形成的规模，才演变成今天这样。

turns.en: So these concepts are age-old is what I would say. What I find with investors is the moment that you start thinking about next generation, how do you invest?
turns.zh: 所以我想说，这些概念其实由来已久。我在投资人身上发现的是，一旦你开始思考下一代、思考'该怎么投资'，

turns.en: How do you think about those things? As distinct from what do I need to do this week, this month, this quarter, it all turns on a long-term orientation.
turns.zh: 该怎么去考虑这些问题？这与'我本周、本月、本季度需要做什么'完全不同——一切都取决于一种长期的取向。

turns.en: What do I think is going on in the long term? How do I think about that? And that juxtaposition between those two things is very different for families who are thinking about next generation and what's going to happen beyond me.
turns.zh: 我认为长期会发生什么？我该如何去想？这种把两件事并置的对比，对那些正在思考下一代、思考'在我之后会发生什么'的家族来说，差异非常大。

turns.en: Have I created something that will go beyond? And that leads you down to make decisions about where do I think this investment that I make today will be 10 years, 20 years from now?
turns.zh: 我是否创造了能够超越我自身、延续下去的东西？这会引导你去做这样的决策：我认为我今天做的这笔投资，10 年后、20 年后会怎样？

turns.en: As distinct from where do I think this investment made today will be next quarter when some new information comes out, etc. And it goes up or down.
turns.zh: 而不是：我认为今天做的这笔投资，下个季度、当某些新消息出来时会怎样，然后它涨涨跌跌。

turns.en: So much more longer-term perspective coming from these families and how they manage their businesses. Of course, as you just touched on, Tucker, the big issue they all face is the generational transition, which is a very critical moment.
turns.zh: 这些家族以及他们经营企业的方式，有着多得多的长期视角。当然，正如你刚才提到的，Tucker，他们共同面对的大问题就是代际交接（generational transition），那是一个极其关键的时刻。

turns.en: You say FX both for the businesses and for the families. Talk us through why that is such a critical moment. It's a critical moment because it's a moment where the founder has to make a decision on two topics.
turns.zh: 我想不管是企业还是家族都是如此，FX。请跟我们讲讲，为什么这是一个如此关键的时刻。它关键，是因为这是创始人必须就两件事做出决策的时刻。

turns.en: Topic number one, should his family, typically his children or any other family members stay involved in the management, typically the running of the business and if so in what capacity?
turns.zh: 第一个议题：他的家族——通常是他的子女或其他家族成员——是否应该继续参与管理，通常是企业的日常经营；如果要，以什么角色参与？

turns.en: And the second decision is how is he or she going to pass on the stock, the ownership of the company from one generation to the next? And what's the organization he set up in order to do that successfully?
turns.zh: 第二个决策是：他要如何将股份、也就是公司的所有权，从一代传给下一代？他为此建立了怎样的组织，才能成功地完成这件事？

turns.en: The statistics you mentioned before that only a third of the businesses pass on to the second generation, about 10% to the third, in our view, in neither good nor bad.
turns.zh: 你之前提到的统计——只有三分之一能传到第二代，大约 10% 能传到第三代——在我们看来，这无所谓好坏。

turns.en: It kind of is what it is. What's important is, does the business benefit from that family ownership or does the business benefit from having a broader ownership base?
turns.zh: 它本来就是如此。重要的是：这家企业从家族所有权中受益，还是从更广泛的股东基础上受益？

turns.en: We have seen outstanding case studies in both. Some businesses with one founder who decided that it absolutely should not stay within the family, diversified the ownership, brought in professional management and the company scale to be enormously successful companies.
turns.zh: 两种情况我们都见过杰出的案例。有些企业由一位创始人创立，他断定企业绝不应该留在家族内部，于是分散了所有权、引入了职业经理人，公司成长为极其成功的企业。

turns.en: And we've seen other examples where the founder took absolutely the reverse view and the business actually tremendously benefited in being controlled and typically also managed by the family.
turns.zh: 我们也见过另一些例子，创始人采取了完全相反的观点，结果企业实际上因为由家族控股、通常也由家族管理而受益匪浅。

turns.en: The key question in our view and experience is, what's the process around this decision making? How early in advance is this considered? And what are the mechanisms to make sure the right judgment or exercise both on the ability of the family to continue to manage and on how to best organize the ownership and make sure the ownership structure and governance survive the passage of time?
turns.zh: 以我们的观点和经验来看，关键问题是：围绕这个决策的过程是怎样的？这个决策提前多久被考虑？又有哪些机制来确保在以下两方面做出正确的判断——家族是否有能力继续经营，以及如何最好地组织所有权——并确保所有权结构和治理能够经受时间的考验？

turns.en: And Tucker, this ultimately all comes down to succession plans. But you found that only about half of the businesses, family businesses, actually have succession plans, but mostly informal and only about a third actually write down these plans.
turns.zh: Tucker，说到底这些都归结到继任计划（succession plan）。但你发现，只有大约一半的家族企业真的有继任计划，而且大多是非正式的，只有大约三分之一真正把计划写了下来。

turns.en: So why is it so hard when this is so critical to their future? I think business succession, like all businesses go through that and the businesses that are well run have a better succession plan.
turns.zh: 那既然它对他们的未来如此关键，为什么还这么难？我认为企业交接是所有企业都要经历的，经营得好的企业通常有更好的继任计划。

turns.en: I think with a family on it's super complicated because it's one thing was what does the founder want? But it's also what does the next generation want?
turns.zh: 我觉得加上家族因素就极其复杂了，因为'创始人想要什么'是一回事，'下一代想要什么'又是另一回事。

turns.en: And the fact is that while business is dynamic and it's impacted by things you can control, but oftentimes things you can't control like the economy, industry, competition, etc.
turns.zh: 而且事实是，商业是动态的，它既受你能控制的东西影响，也经常受你控制不了的东西影响，比如经济、行业、竞争等等。

turns.en: Families are impacted that way too. And families change and grow. The next generation tends to get married to other people, which brings other people into the mix, etc.
turns.zh: 家族也会以同样的方式受到影响。家族会变化、会壮大。下一代往往会和外人结婚，这就把其他人带进了这个体系，等等。

turns.en: So all of these things make it very complicated. It's certainly a best practice to write some things down. We would agree with that. But what is written down and the flexibility around what is written down to be able to adapt to new circumstances and things that come down the bike is vitally important.
turns.zh: 所以这一切都让它变得非常复杂。把事情写下来当然是最佳实践，这点我们也认同。但写下什么，以及围绕所写内容保留多大的灵活性，好去适应新的情况和未来冒出来的变数，这一点至关重要。

turns.en: And so having a plan is a really good thing from a structure standpoint. But it's also a really good thing to make sure this flexibility built in to allow for things that will inevitably occur.
turns.zh: 所以从结构的角度看，有这样一个计划是很好的事。但同样重要的是，要确保把灵活性内建进去，为那些必然会发生的事情留有余地。

turns.en: I wanted to just pick up on your question, Alisson. In my experience, many of these founder-owners tend initially certainly in their lifetime to be extremely busy, extremely preoccupied and engaged in their business and often prioritize their business over long-term planning.
turns.zh: 我想就你的问题接着说几句，Allison。以我的经验，很多创始人兼所有者——至少在他们在世的时候——往往极度忙碌，全身心扑在自己的企业上，常常把企业放在长期规划之前。

turns.en: Often this is for the right reason to the great benefit of the business. And then the second key factor is orchestrating and considering this decision forces some pretty hard judgments.
turns.zh: 这往往是出于正确的理由，对企业大有裨益。然后第二个关键因素是，统筹协调、认真考虑这个决策，会迫使他们做出一些相当艰难的判断。

turns.en: Some of which they're able to do at a certain point in time, some of which they'd rather have more time to consider, including either family or the children capable to have the relevant experience and desire to be involved in the business.
turns.zh: 有些判断他们能在某个时点上做出，有些他们宁可再多些时间去考虑，包括判断家族成员、子女当中谁具备相关经验、又有意愿参与到企业里。

turns.en: In some cases it's too early to judge. Many of these founders decide that taking more time and having more visibility with the passage of time will de-risk some of these decisions.
turns.zh: 有些情况下现在判断还太早。很多创始人认为，多花些时间、随着时间推移看得更清楚，能降低某些决策的风险。

turns.en: And as you said, FX, it's a process because you have these creators, they're focused on growing their business. But at some point they do transition to thinking about how the business is going to outlive them.
turns.zh: 正如 FX 你说的，这是一个过程，因为这些创造企业的人专注于做大自己的生意，但在某个阶段，他们确实会转向思考：这家企业如何能比自己活得更久。

turns.en: So what does that transition look like, especially for families that do this well? That process really involves facing those two questions. Should my family, any family members be involved in the business itself in a management role, junior or senior, about over time senior?
turns.zh: 那这种转变具体是什么样的，尤其是那些做得好的家族？那个过程其实就是要直面那两个问题：我的家族、我的家族成员，是否应该以管理角色参与企业本身——无论初级还是高级，还是随着时间推移成为高级角色？

turns.en: Yes or no? And how do I organize the ownership to be transferred from one generation to the other? On the first one, my own view is it's a very delicate judgment but really relies on is there someone who is capable, who has the relevant experience and who has a desire to rise up to the occasion?
turns.zh: 是还是不是？还有，我如何安排所有权的代际转移？关于第一个，我个人的看法是，这是一个非常微妙的判断，但关键在于：是否存在一个有能力、有相关经验、又愿意迎难而上的人？

turns.en: That judgment needs to be as independent as possible. Typically the founder is the absolute best person to render that judgment. In some cases we see them soliciting external input to benchmark or compare their own family members with external talent.
turns.zh: 这个判断需要尽可能独立。通常创始人是做出这个判断最合适的人。有些情况下，我们会看到他们征求外部意见，把自己的家族成员与外部人才做对标或比较。

turns.en: And what we find on average is the larger the company, the more global, the more complex, typically the more likely it will require a non-family member with significant experience to continue to run it and we see many family businesses choosing to bring professional management as a scale up.
turns.zh: 我们发现，平均而言，公司越大、越全球化、越复杂，就越可能需要一位经验丰富的非家族成员来继续经营它；我们看到很多家族企业随着规模扩大，选择引入职业经理人。

turns.en: On the second, which is a question of how does the ownership get passed on? The initial typical approach is to say let's divide the ownership equally between the number of children or sort of second generation family members.
turns.zh: 关于第二个问题——所有权如何传承下去？最初常见的做法是，把所有权在所有子女、或者说第二代家族成员之间平均分配。

turns.en: The question that brings is what's the organization of that group? How large is that group? Has any member got the right to exit if she wants to or he wants to and what's the mechanism to exit?
turns.zh: 随之而来的问题是：这个群体的组织方式是什么？这个群体有多大？任何成员如果想退出——无论她或他——是否有退出权，退出的机制是什么？

turns.en: And how do any conflicts get tackled and resolved? Is this within the family or is this with a governance structure that allows the resolution of conflict?
turns.zh: 又该如何应对和解决可能出现的冲突？是在家族内部解决，还是通过一个能够化解冲突的治理结构来解决？

turns.en: In my experience, this process and this mechanism needs to be thought through early on before the number of family members gets too large and typically having some exit right of some form and having some conflict resolution mechanism in case there is one or disagreement on any point goes a long way.
turns.zh: 以我的经验，这个过程和机制需要在家族成员数量变得过于庞大之前就及早想清楚。通常，拥有某种形式的退出权，以及针对任何一点上可能出现的争议有某种解决冲突的机制，会大有帮助。

turns.en: And as we touched on, it's not necessarily just about the family dynamics. There's a whole world, there's an economic cycle because ultimately they can pass on and keep the business in the family but there's also the ability to IPO, there's the ability to sell outright.
turns.zh: 正如我们前面提到的，这不一定只是家族内部动态的问题。外面还有一个更广阔的世界，有经济周期。因为最终他们可以选择传承、把企业留在家族里，但也可以选择 IPO，或者整体出售。

turns.en: So how big of a driver are these other factors when you're talking to families as they work through this? In many cases, one of the questions the company faces and the family faces is does the company need external capital to scale the business?
turns.zh: 当你在家族处理这些问题的过程中与他们交谈时，这些其他因素的影响有多大？在很多情况下，企业和家族共同面对的问题之一是：这家企业是否需要外部资本来扩大业务规模？

turns.en: And typically when there is a capital need, it brings the question of who are the investors, what's the source of capital and by how much should the family get diluted as part of that?
turns.zh: 通常，一旦有资本需求，就会带来这样一些问题：谁是投资人，资本从哪里来，家族在这个过程中应该被稀释多少？

turns.en: That's one big aspect. A second aspect and we've seen numerous examples of this is a number of families decide and believe that bringing a third party investor, whether it's a single investor or a group of investors and it could also be the public market, can be a source of discipline and a forcing mechanism around many aspects that may be complicated to discuss or resolve within the family.
turns.zh: 这是一个大的层面。第二个层面，我们也见过很多例子：一些家族认定并相信，引入第三方投资人——无论是单个投资人还是一群投资人，甚至可以是公开市场——能够带来一种约束，并成为推动解决问题的一种机制，而这些方面在家族内部往往很难讨论或很难解决。

turns.en: Some choose to sell other because they believe it's the right thing for their business or the right thing for the family. What I have witnessed many times in the context of the sale is there could be great economic outcome and great solutions for businesses to be consolidated, merged or sold, but that often the family has part of its identity in the business and the sale has a significant impact on the family's emotions
turns.zh: 有些选择出售，是因为他们相信这对他们的企业或对家族来说是正确的。在出售的情境里，我多次看到：企业被整合、被并购或被出售，可能带来很好的经济结果、很好的方案；但家族往往把一部分自我认同寄托在企业上，所以出售会强烈冲击家族的情感，

turns.en: and on their sense of identity that's tied to the business. I'll just tack on to that from FX, both expertise but also if you will, the objective is to take care of the health and well-being of the business.
turns.zh: 以及他们与企业紧密相连的身份认同感。我想接着 FX 说的补充一点，不仅是他的专业领域，也可以说，他的目标是呵护企业的健康与福祉。

turns.en: In doing that, he's interacting directly with the founder slash CEO. It's a different element about I'll call it the health and well-being of the family and what's in their best interest and sometimes it's aligned and sometimes it's not.
turns.zh: 在这个过程中，他直接和创始人兼 CEO 打交道。而那是一个不同的维度——我把它称为家族的健康与福祉，什么对他们最有利，有时候这和企业的利益是一致的，有时候并不一致。

turns.en: I think the other thing too for any succession planning or any long-term capital structure planning, that also changes over time and so this concept of we're going to make a plan and then we're good, it doesn't apply, it needs to be reviewed and stress tested regularly.
turns.zh: 我觉得还有一点，任何继任规划或长期的资本结构规划，都会随时间而变化。所以'我们做一个计划就万事大吉'这种想法并不成立，它需要定期地重新审视和压力测试。

turns.en: In the same way as you think about next generation planning, most parents when they think about their children, it's a different set of circumstances when they're 35 than when they're five and how to think about that and so again, it's a regular review of where we are in the process.
turns.zh: 就像你思考下一代规划一样，大多数父母在为孩子做打算时，孩子 35 岁和孩子 5 岁时是完全不同的情形，该怎么去想这件事？所以同样，需要对'我们在整个过程的哪一步'做定期回顾。

turns.en: Tucker, I think you raised just an excellent point on this which is typically in the first generation, the interests of the business are very aligned and mirror the interests of the family.
turns.zh: Tucker，你这一点提得非常好，通常在第一代，企业的利益和家族的利益高度一致，几乎是相互映照的。

turns.en: It's one individual, it's his business and that's his life or her life. As a number of generation passes, the family's interests may differ from the business interests and being very clear on whether that's the case, where do they align and where do they differ is step number one in long-term planning.
turns.zh: 那是同一个人，是他的企业，那是他的生命、她的生命。但随着一代代过去，家族的利益可能与企业的利益产生分歧，所以在长期规划里，第一步就是非常清楚地判断：是不是这种情况，哪些地方一致，哪些地方分歧。

turns.en: Right. On the same line, that founder is the shareholder and so what they want to do for the business and what they want to do for their wealth creation is the same and many founders say one of the things I want to do with this is I want to give this business to the next generation.
turns.zh: 是的。沿着同样的思路，创始人本身就是股东，所以他想为企业做的事，和想为自己财富增值做的事，是一回事。很多创始人会说，我拿这一切想做的一件事，就是把这家企业传给下一代。

turns.en: There are other founders who say what I want to do is I want to give the advantages that I have to the next generation but I want them to do something different or whatever they want or et cetera and all of those things.
turns.zh: 也有其他创始人会说，我想做的是把我拥有的优势传给下一代，但我希望他们去做别的事情，或者做他们想做的任何事，如此种种。

turns.en: Again, as that next generation grows, the complexity around that grows as well. So that gets to the wealth creation aspect of this Tucker, which you have a lot of insight into because ultimately the day a founder sells the company or takes it public, they end up with wealth and basically becomes like this pile of money that they have never had to manage before versus a business that they were managing day in and day out.
turns.zh: 再次强调，随着下一代人数增多，围绕这一点的复杂性也会增加。这就触及到财富创造这一块了，Tucker，你对这一块有很多洞见。因为说到底，创始人出售公司或让公司上市的那一天，他们手中就有了财富，本质上变成了一大堆钱，而这笔钱他们以前从来没管理过，不像那家他们每天、每时每刻在经营的企业。

turns.en: How do the largest families navigate this and handle this? Well, it's not necessarily what they started out for but it is an outcome of the success they have and how they think about that, how they think about the way an endowment would think about what is this money for, what is its purpose, what are the other not only wealth that I want to pass along but what are the values I want to pass along and all of that comes into the thing.
turns.zh: 那些最大的家族是如何驾驭、如何处理这件事的？嗯，财富未必是他们最初的出发点，但那是他们成功的一个结果。他们怎么看待这一点，怎么像捐赠基金（endowment）那样去思考——这笔钱是为了什么、它的目的是什么、除了我想传承的财富之外，还有我想传承的价值观——这些全都融入了这件事当中。

turns.en: And yes, so the mindset does change over time. And not just the mindset, the organizational structure, the resources required to manage this wealth that is now outside the business versus in the business changes.
turns.zh: 是的，心态确实会随时间改变。而且不只是心态，组织架构、以及管理这笔现在已经在企业之外的财富——而不是在企业之内的财富——所需的资源，也在改变。

turns.en: For sure. And I think it's varied how that works. Some people say, well, I want to set up now a new business whose job it is to manage the wealth that I created.
turns.zh: 当然。我觉得这做法因人而异。有的人会说，好，我想现在新设一家企业，专门负责管理我创造出来的这笔财富。

turns.en: Others would say, I don't aspire to be in that business. I realize that I have to, quote, take care of these resources in a different way than when it was all in the business and they go in different routes.
turns.zh: 另一些人会说，我不想去做这一行。我意识到，我不得不——用他们的话说——用一种不同于过去所有财富都放在企业里时的方式来打理这些资源，于是他们走上不同的路径。

turns.en: And the reality is this is what's very interesting about the roles that we get to play is it runs the range. There isn't everybody does it this way or that way.
turns.zh: 现实情况是这样的——我们扮演的角色最有趣的地方在于，它覆盖了整个光谱。并不存在所有人都按这一种或那一种方式来做。

turns.en: Think about different things. And again, that's where family comes into play as well. Alisson, if I just can add one thing on this. We're also seeing in this process often important differences between first generation family members who are involved in the business and who often have limited time or choose to spend limited time on allocating or managing the capital that's outside the business versus the second generation and onwards who inherit a lot of wealth and a lot of capital
turns.zh: 大家考虑的东西各不相同。而且如前所说，这也是家族因素发挥作用的地方。Allison，关于这一点，如果我可以补充一句的话：我们在这个过程中也常常看到，参与企业的第一代家族成员，往往时间有限，或者选择只把有限的时间花在配置、管理企业外部资本上；而第二代及以后的家族成员继承了大量的财富和资本，这两者之间存在重要的差异。

turns.en: and who's one of the important projects but also responsibilities is to be good steward of this capital. And Tucker and his team have a lot of experience with the dynamic between the first generation, the second generation and the amount of time and effort and resources that each individual family members or branches choose to or want to spend in managing their own assets.
turns.zh: 对他们来说，成为这笔资本的良好守护者，既是一项重要任务，也是一种责任。Tucker 和他的团队对第一代与第二代之间的这种动态——以及每个家族成员或每个家族分支在自己资产管理上选择或愿意投入多少时间、精力和资源——有着非常丰富的经验。

turns.en: We end this conversation how we began it with this long-term mindset that these families have but to your point, Tucker, with some flexibility so that they can adapt to the changing family and business dynamics.
turns.zh: 我们结束这场对话的方式，和我们开始它时一样——带着这些家族拥有的那种长期心态，但正如你所说，Tucker，也要有某种灵活性，好让他们能够适应不断变化的家族与企业动态。

turns.en: But in some ways, my takeaway is in a way, as we talk to our individual investors, people potentially listening to this podcast, there is always an emphasis on long-term planning for your own wealth that those who plan and think about this succession ultimately end up in a better spot than those who don't.
turns.zh: 但某种程度上，我的收获是这样：正如我们对个人投资者、对可能在听这期播客的人所说的那样，我们一直强调要为自己的财富做长期规划，那些真正去做规划、去思考传承的人，最终的处境往往比不做的人更好。

turns.en: Is that a takeaway here about thinking about always having that long-term plan in your mind? I think it absolutely is. People say long-term oriented, that's a better way to be.
turns.zh: 这算不算一个启示——要始终在心中有那个长期计划？我觉得完全算。人们说'要长期取向'，那是一种更好的状态。

turns.en: But if you take a step back, we live in an incredibly short-term oriented world and so it's hard to push against that the way money is managed.
turns.zh: 但如果你退一步看，我们生活在一个极其短期导向的世界里，所以要对抗这种现状很难——资金的运作方式就是如此。

turns.en: It's nice to be able to see your stock that you own go up and down in price. But if it goes up a lot, you're tempted to sell then you pay taxes and you have to figure out what to do with it again.
turns.zh: 能看到你持有的股票忽涨忽跌也挺好的。但如果它涨了很多，你就忍不住想卖，一卖就要交税，然后你又得重新想这笔钱该怎么办。

turns.en: If you're in a private company or a private equity, you're holding it for a longer period of time but then you don't have the flexibility if you need the money to do this thing.
turns.zh: 如果你投的是非上市公司或者私募股权，你会持有更长时间，但如果你需要用钱去做某件事时，你反而没有那种灵活性。

turns.en: What I would argue is it leans towards people should be thinking about staying consistently invested. And a safer way to do that is to not just own one thing but to own a portfolio of things so that on average the market goes higher over a period of time if you believe in global GDP growth.
turns.zh: 我想主张的是，人们应当考虑持续保持投资。更安全的做法是——不只是持有一样东西，而是持有一整个投资组合，这样只要你对全球 GDP 的增长有信心，长期来看市场平均是向上的。

turns.en: But that to me is the takeaway. These extraordinary families that have built the enterprises that FX deals with regularly, they have made concentrated bets in one basically company that becomes a stock and that's a way for tremendous wealth creation but it's incredibly risky.
turns.zh: 但对我来说这就是要点所在。那些非凡的家族，建立了 FX 日常打交道的那些企业，他们做的其实是集中的赌注——押在一家基本上变成了股票的公司上，这是创造巨大财富的一种方式，但也极其冒险。

turns.en: And the things that we don't talk about on podcasts like that are the many other people who tried that and it didn't work. And so again, you blend the two together, it's owning equity but doing it in a diversified way and saying consistently long or invested.
turns.zh: 我们在像这样的播客里不太会讲的是，还有很多其他人也试过这么做，结果却没成。所以再一次，你把两者融合起来——持有权益类资产，但用分散的方式，并且始终做多、始终处于投资状态。

turns.en: Effect anything to add in terms of a closing message? I fully agree and what we've seen is many of these entrepreneurs that have created extraordinary businesses have played the long game.
turns.zh: FX，收尾之际，还有什么要补充的吗？我完全同意，我们看到的是，很多这些缔造了非凡企业的企业家，玩的都是长期主义这一手。

turns.en: They have deployed capital, they have adjusted and adapted their business and investment decision through many cycles including volatile times but they remain invested and many of those and many families that have benefited from this is not only to remain invested but to continue to invest whether it's adding capital, buying back stock in the market in their own businesses through the cycle to increase their ownership.
turns.zh: 他们投入资本，穿越许多周期——包括市场动荡的时期——不断调整、适应他们的经营和投资决策，但始终保持在场。很多从中受益的家族所做的，不仅是不离场，而且是持续投资，无论是追加资本，还是在这一周期里在公开市场上回购自己企业的股票、增持所有权。

turns.en: So these are very concentrated bets but when you have very disciplined long-term steward of capital that know and understand the business and are able to attract and retain great management and make disciplined decisions with respect to their family ownership you typically have a winning recipe for great success and great value creation.
turns.zh: 所以这些是非常集中的赌注，但当你拥有一群极其自律、长期守护资本、又深谙这门生意的人，他们能够吸引并留住优秀的管理团队，在家族持股问题上做出自律的决策时，你通常就拥有了一张通向巨大成功和巨大价值创造的制胜配方。

turns.en: FX Tucker, thanks so much for joining us and sharing your insights on this. Really interesting, probably not talked enough about sector of the markets and the economy given its size and impact so thanks again.
turns.zh: FX、Tucker，非常感谢你们加入、分享你们的洞见。这个话题真的很有意思，而且考虑到它的规模和影响力，这可能是市场上、经济中被谈论得还不够多的一个领域，再次感谢。
